It turns a missing resource into an HTTP 403 via HttpException. All real work goes to application services (AccountService.account, AccountBalanceService.createOrUpdateAccountBalance, accountBalance and deleteAccountBalance). There is no persistence logic: no Prisma client calls or query construction. The ownership checks (look up a record by the user's id, return 403 if it isn't found) are request-scoped access control. Handling these at the transport boundary is normal for a controller. They contain no business rule about balances. The Prisma AccountBalance type is used only as a return type, which falls under import direction and is out of scope.
